paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this little letter is built on: truth and love belong together. The elder loves the lady and her children "in the truth," and he says it twice that truth and love go hand in hand (2 John 1:1, 3). He says love is this: "that we walk according to His commandments" (2 John 1:6). So love isn't just a warm feeling, friend. It's walking the way God said to walk, and that walk is as old as "the beginning."

Then comes the warning, and it matters just as much. The elder says many deceivers refuse to confess "the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh" (2 John 1:7). He wants them to hold on to the teaching of Christ, because "Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son" (2 John 1:9). I'll be honest, I have pulled a batch early in my life and it NEVER ends well, but the lesson here is bigger than cookies: don't run ahead of what Christ taught, and don't let go of it either.

So what do you do with that, baker? Keep loving, and keep your feet on what you've been taught about Jesus. Hold both, because one without the other leaves you lopsided, like a cookie with all chips on one side. And notice how the elder ends: he wants to come and speak face to face, "so that our joy may be complete" (2 John 1:12). Truth and love aren't meant to be carried alone, friend. They're meant to be walked together, with people you can look in the eye.
